reading_commitments: Reading is decoding; legitimate instruction makes the alphabetic principle explicit through systematic phonics
Reading is meaning-making; legitimate instruction immerses children in authentic literature, allowing decoding to emerge naturally
Reading requires both decoding and meaning-making; legitimate instruction balances explicit phonics with authentic literature exposure
Reading instruction must be designed for the most vulnerable learners first; legitimate instruction follows explicit, cumulative, diagnostic principles from structured literacy
axiom_bases: Phonics reading grounds legitimacy in making the code explicit before meaning; whole-language reading grounds legitimacy in meaning-making from which code knowledge emerges. No single framework can hold both 'explicit-first' and 'emergent-from-meaning' as simultaneously true about the same developmental process.

Structured literacy reading holds that vulnerable learners require maximum explicitness and structure as the baseline; whole-language reading holds that all learners benefit from authentic meaning-making contexts with minimal imposed structure. No framework can hold both 'structure-first-for-all' and 'meaning-first-for-all' as true.

reading_commitments: Reading acquisition requires explicit, systematic instruction in phoneme-grapheme correspondence before connected text exposure; decoding precedes and enables comprehension

Reading acquisition emerges from meaningful engagement with connected text; phonics skills develop naturally through exposure and context; explicit decoding instruction is unnecessary and potentially harmful to reading motivation
Reading acquisition requires both systematic phonics instruction AND meaningful text engagement; the two are complementary rather than contradictory; instructional balance is the key

Reading acquisition requires explicit, systematic, cumulative instruction in phonological awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension; designed for students with dyslexia but applicable universally; Orton-Gillingham tradition
axiom_bases: Phonics_reading axiom: decoding skill is prerequisite to comprehension (bottom-up processing). Whole_language_reading axiom: comprehension drives decoding skill development (top-down processing). No single coherent framework holds both as simultaneously true—one must be causally prior.

Phonics_reading axiom: systematic explicit instruction is necessary and sufficient. Balanced_literacy_reading axiom: systematic instruction is necessary but not sufficient (meaningful text engagement also required). A framework holding phonics_reading's sufficiency claim cannot simultaneously hold balanced_literacy's insufficiency claim.

reading_commitments: Reading acquisition requires explicit systematic instruction in grapheme-phoneme correspondence as foundational skill
Reading acquisition occurs through meaningful engagement with authentic texts; decoding skills emerge implicitly from exposure
Reading acquisition requires both explicit phonics and authentic literature exposure in integrated practice
axiom_bases: Phonics axiom (alphabetic principle must be explicitly taught as prerequisite) contradicts whole-language axiom (meaning-making drives skill emergence). No coherent framework holds both: either decoding is foundational or it is derivative.

reading_commitments: Reliable decarbonization requires dispatchable baseload power that renewables cannot provide at scale
Renewables plus storage can achieve full decarbonization faster and cheaper than nuclear
Optimal decarbonization requires technology-neutral portfolio including both nuclear and renewables
Decarbonization requires demand reduction making large-scale generation expansion unnecessary
axiom_bases: Baseload reading holds that grid physics requires dispatchable generation as foundational constraint; renewable primacy reading holds that storage plus demand response can substitute fully. No single framework accepts both the irreducibility of baseload and its eliminability.

Portfolio reading accepts growth-compatible energy expansion as legitimate climate response; degrowth reading holds that expansion itself perpetuates unsustainability. No framework simultaneously validates technology-neutral expansion and rejects expansion as category.

reading_commitments: Mitigation requires maximizing all low-carbon sources; nuclear is necessary for reliable baseload
Mitigation requires fastest deployment per dollar; nuclear's capital intensity and timeline make it net-harmful
Mitigation requires transforming energy systems toward decentralization and democratic control; nuclear perpetuates extractive centralization
axiom_bases: Portfolio reading holds 'all low-carbon sources are complementary' as axiomatic; opportunity-cost reading holds 'capital scarcity makes nuclear and renewables substitutes' as axiomatic. No single framework can hold both: either capital is abundant enough for portfolio diversification (A) or scarce enough that nuclear crowds out renewables (B).

Portfolio reading treats governance structure as orthogonal to mitigation effectiveness; systems-transition reading treats centralized vs democratic control as constitutive of what counts as mitigation. No framework can hold both: either mitigation is technology-neutral (A) or governance structure is part of the climate problem (B).

reading_commitments: A technology is legitimate for climate mitigation if and only if it provides dispatchable, baseload-capable generation to ensure grid stability
A technology is legitimate for climate mitigation if and only if it can be deployed at scale within the remaining carbon budget timeline (2030/2050 targets)
A technology is legitimate for climate mitigation if and only if its worst-case failure modes and legacy costs are bounded and reversible within a generation
axiom_bases: No single framework can hold both 'grid stability is the binding constraint' and 'deployment speed is the binding constraint' as simultaneously true. One must be subordinated to the other in any coherent policy.

No single framework can hold both 'accept irreversible legacy costs for grid stability' and 'reject technologies with irreversible legacy costs' as simultaneously true. These axioms are mutually exclusive.

Velocity primacy accepts intermittency risk and storage uncertainty to maximize deployment speed; precautionary reading rejects technologies whose failure modes are not fully characterized. A coherent framework cannot hold both as binding constraints.

reading_commitments: Software freedom is a moral imperative; users have inherent rights to control their computing
Open source is a superior development methodology that produces better software through collaborative peer review
Software is intellectual property; creators have legitimate rights to control distribution and extract value
Software is collective knowledge infrastructure requiring active stewardship against enclosure
axiom_bases: Freedom imperative holds that users have inherent moral rights to software source code that override creator property claims; property rights reading holds that creators have legitimate exclusion rights that override user access claims. No single framework can simultaneously hold both as foundational axioms.

Pragmatic openness treats source availability as contingent optimization (acceptable to choose proprietary when outcomes warrant); freedom imperative treats it as categorical moral requirement (never acceptable to deny). A consequentialist framework cannot simultaneously hold a practice as both contingently optimal and categorically required.

reading_commitments: Software control is a matter of fundamental user freedom; proprietary software is ethically illegitimate because it denies users control over their computing
Software control is a development methodology choice; open source produces better software through peer review and collaboration, but proprietary models are legitimate alternatives
Software control is a property right; creators have legitimate authority to restrict use, modification, and distribution to protect investment and enable commercial sustainability
Software control is a commons governance question; neither absolute freedom nor absolute property but negotiated collective management of shared digital infrastructure
axiom_bases: Freedom imperative holds that users have inalienable right to control their computing; property rights holds that creators have legitimate authority to deny that control. No single framework can hold both as simultaneously valid foundational axioms.

Freedom imperative treats proprietary software as categorically illegitimate (ethical violation); pragmatic openness treats it as a legitimate alternative methodology. No framework can simultaneously hold proprietary software as both ethically impermissible and methodologically acceptable.

reading_commitments: Software freedom is a fundamental ethical requirement; proprietary software is an injustice
Open source is a superior development methodology; freedom is instrumental to quality
Software is intellectual property; creators have legitimate right to restrict access and modification
Software licensing should maximize aggregate welfare; both models serve different contexts
axiom_bases: Freedom imperative holds that users have inalienable rights to source access that cannot be legitimately restricted; property rights reading holds that creators have legitimate authority to impose such restrictions. No single framework can hold both axioms simultaneously.

Freedom imperative treats proprietary software as categorically unjust regardless of consequences; utilitarian hybrid treats justice as context-dependent and outcome-based. A deontological framework cannot simultaneously hold that an action is categorically wrong and that its permissibility depends on aggregate welfare calculations.
